svg.text: The machine is grey cast plastic; the people are wood. Threat escalates by silhouette: flat → cross → tower. Damage is the people's repair work: tangerine wooden clamps.
THE MACHINE · threat pieces, one grey plastic
hex nut, lying flat · 10 mm · health 1
cog on its edge, axle peg · 14 mm · health 2
cracked vacuum tube, pinched neck · 23 mm · health 3
Side and top views differ for every piece:
nut = hexagon, cog = cross, tube = circle, Crew = ring.
DAMAGE STATES · mid-turn, cleared at Time passes

Each point of damage on a threat piece is one repair clamp. When the clamps would reach its health, the piece is destroyed (and the clamps go back to the pool). Glitch has health 1: any damage removes it.
Fault: 1 clamp on the axle peg
Failure: up to 2 C-clips snapped onto the neck
a clamp shows; count from the side
lockout tag leans on the piece
THE PEOPLE · wood, brass and slag
wooden pawn, fishbowl helmet · 16 mm · health 2
stained wooden rocket nose cones · 10 mm
slag lump, never two the same · 12 mm
the players' marks on the machine
ON THE BOARD · mid-turn, on every section colour (pieces at 55 %)
Open question for the designer: on a downgrade (Failure → Fault), does the damage carry over? Suggested: it does, capped at the new piece's health − 1.
Print-and-play: Glitch, Crew, influence and Decay die-cut to their top outline; Fault and Failure as small standees; clamps as tangerine chits under the base; injured Crew flipped face-down.
